This application has been filed on behalf of the Appellant Salman Ansari S/o Nanhe Mistri under Section 389 Cr.P.C. seeking suspension of sentence during pendency of the present appeal arising out of a case FIR No.217/2017 under Section 6 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act,
2012 ('POCSO Act'), registered at PS: KN Katju Marg, Delhi.

sentences.text: Appellant has challenged in the present appeal the impugned judgment dated 18.02.2020 whereby he has been convicted for offence under Section 376(2)(f) & (i) IPC and Section 6 of POCSO Act.

Challenge is also laid to the order on sentence dated 03.09.2020 whereby Appellant has been sentenced to RI for 12 years along with fine of Rs.5,000/- for offence punishable under Section 376(2)(f) & (i) IPC and RI for 12 years along with fine of Rs.10,000/- for offence punishable under Section 6 of POCSO Act

All substantive sentences are to run concurrently.

2. Learned Senior counsel for the Appellant contends that Appellant has served more than half of the sentence awarded as he has already undergone 7 years and 2 months of the sentence including remission.

Reliance is placed on the orders of the Supreme Court in Sonadhar v. The State of Chhattisgarh, 2021 SCC OnLine SC 3182 and Saudan Singh v. State of Uttar Pradesh, 2021 SCC Salman Ansari vs State (Nct) Of Delhi & Anr

Reliance is also placed on the observation of the Supreme Court in Satender Kumar Antil v. Central Bureau of Investigation and Another, (2022) 10 SCC 51, to the effect that amongst other factors, delay in taking up the main appeal ought to be considered for a favourable release on bail.

It is urged that the Co-ordinate Benches of this Court in Dablu Kumar v. State, Crl. A. No.399/2021, date of decision 06.11.2023; Amar Singh v. The State, Crl. A. No.519/2022, date of decision 07.11.2023; Sonu Kumar and Ors. v. The State (Govt. of NCT of Delhi), Crl. A. No.338/2022, date of decision 20.11.2023;
Harvansh v. State of NCT Delhi, Crl. A. No.343/2021, date of decision 20.11.2023; and in several other cases have suspended the sentences during the pendency of the appeals, where the periods undergone by the respective convicts were more than 50% of the sentences awarded.

Appellant has a good case on merits and there is a high possibility of the appeal being allowed in his favour.

On merits, it is inter alia contended that mother of the victim refused to get internal examination of the victim, which finds endorsed on the MLC and is supported by the testimony of PW-4 Dr. Manila Yadav and there is thus no medical evidence to corroborate the testimony of the victim.
In fact, it is recorded that during the medical examination, mother of the victim made a categorical statement that there was no 'indruni ched chaad'.
Trial Court has also failed to appreciate the testimony of PW-2 Ms. Meenu Goyal, who deposed that Appellant was not the dance teacher of the victim.
DW-2 Ms. Pooja deposed that she was the one teaching dance to students between 3 to 5 years of age and during the classes, one Ms.
Priya and
a maid were always present.

Appellant has been falsely implicated on account of past rivalry between the uncle of the victim and the Appellant on account of a dispute relating to a choreography event at a wedding in the year 2016.
There are several instances which show that victim was tutored into giving the statements against the Appellant.
It is further urged that Appellant has no criminal antecedents and his jail conduct is 'satisfactory'.

It is candidly submitted that earlier application for suspension of sentence was dismissed by this Court on 24.08.2023,
however, subsequently the Court had observed that if the appeal cannot be taken up for hearing, it would be open for the Appellant to seek suspension of sentence.
4.

Learned APP for the State opposes the application for suspension of sentence on the ground that the allegations against the Appellant are serious and a similar application was dismissed by this Court by a detailed order dated 24.08.2023.
It is argued that it is wrong for the learned Senior counsel This is a digitally signed order.

sentences.text: While considering the application, the Court is required to consider various other factors and some of them are seriousness of allegations, age of the victim, severity of the punishment, etc.
In none of the cases cited on behalf of the Appellant, conviction was under Section 376(2)(f) & (i) IPC or Section 6 of the POCSO Act, which are heinous offences.
The victim child identified the Appellant as the person who committed the assault and there is no contradiction in the testimony of the material prosecution witnesses.
In any case, appreciation of evidence can only be done at the time of final hearing of the appeal and not at this stage.

5. Heard learned Senior counsel for the Appellant and learned APP for the State.
6.
Nominal roll has been requisitioned which supports the plea of the Appellant that he has already undergone 7 years and 2 months of the sentence awarded including remission.
Appellant has no criminal antecedents and his jail conduct is 'satisfactory'.

Order sheets indicate that despite endeavour made on every date to hear the appeal finally, the same could not be taken up and since the hearing of the appeal is likely to take further time, without adverting to the merits of the case and in view of the observations of the Supreme Court in Sonadhar (supra) and Saudan Singh (supra), wherein it has been held that in cases other than the ones concerning life sentences, broad parameter of 50% of actual sentence undergone can be the basis of granting bail, this Court deems it fit to suspend the sentence of the Appellant during the pendency of the appeal.

This Court also finds strength from the judgment of the Supreme Court in Bhagwan Rama Shinde Gosai and Others v.
State of Gujarat, (1999) 4

7. Accordingly, the present application is allowed and sentence of the Appellant is suspended during the pendency of the present appeal.

It is directed that Appellant be released on bail, subject to his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- with two sureties of the like amount to the satisfaction of the Trial Court, out of which one surety will be by a person who is a permanent resident of Delhi.

He shall provide his mobile number to the IO concerned and keep the same active at all times and shall not change the mobile number without prior intimation to the IO and the Trial Court;
iii.

He shall furnish his permanent residential address to the concerned IO and shall intimate the IO as well as the Trial Court by filing an affidavit regarding any change Salman Ansari vs State (Nct) Of Delhi & Anr on 16 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/29378660/
